subject: Pricing & packaging check — OptiCart RFP: competitor parity matrix
messages:
From: Amira Hassan <amira.hassan@opticart.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@opticart.com>, procurement@opticart.com
Date: 2026-08-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: hosted API pricing + competitor parity request

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking the call earlier — putting the request in writing so our procurement and engineering leads have a single source of truth. OptiCart is finalizing vendors for a hosted text-generation API to power search & personalization. As part of our RFP we'd like: 1) a baseline hosted API rate card (per-token gen, per-embedding) for your hosted product; 2) any standard packaging or committed-discount tiers; and 3) a short competitor parity note showing how your hosted economics stack up against OpenAI, Anthropic, Together, and AWS (we care about median 2k-token prompt latency and unit cost at 50k qps-equivalent tokens/day).

Deliverable ideally by end of week so we can include in the vendor comparison matrix. Attached is our internal rate request template for your convenience (OptiCart_Rate_Request_v1.pdf). If you have a quick template or a short bullet response that points to an internal ratecard, that works too.

Main negotiation points for our team:
- Ability to match or beat OpenAI GPT-like per-token rates for high-volume usage
- Clear committed-spend discounts and early-termination terms
- Data residency + audit evidence for enterprise customers (SOC/SLA language)

Thanks — we may loop in legal next week depending on pricing.

Best,
Amira Hassan
Head of Procurement, OptiCart
amira.hassan@opticart.com
+1 415-555-0132
From: priya_natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Amira Hassan <amira.hassan@opticart.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: hosted API pricing + competitor parity request

Hi Amira — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. We're happy to provide the baseline rates and a short competitive note. I'll loop in Marcus (pricing) and Evelyn (solutions/enterprise) to draft a concise matrix comparing Redwood hosted economics vs OpenAI / Anthropic / Together / AWS.

Quick operational context so our response is aligned with what you care about:
- Our hosted tier supports streaming and function/tool calling natively; per-token rates differ for streaming vs non-streaming in long-form workloads.
- For high-volume customers we typically evaluate a reserved capacity (Dedicated) commitment which drives deeper unit discounts — we can show equivalence in effective per-token cost for a given commit.
- Any compliance evidence (SOC2, KMS integrations) is available; we will include pointers to the audit pack rather than sending raw docs.

I'll aim to send the ratecard + parity note by EOD Friday PST. If OptiCart can share a target committed monthly spend range (or the number you referenced on the call), that will let us tailor the tiers.

— Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Amira Hassan <amira.hassan@opticart.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@opticart.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed baseline + competitor note for OptiCart (draft)

Priya / team — draft attached: redwood_proposed_ratecard_v2.xlsx. Below are the high-level bullets I'd include in the parity note to answer the RFP items succinctly. Feel free to trim for external.

1) Baseline hosted rates (public, non-committed):
- Generation (text): $0.0009 / token (standard endpoint, billed per 1k tokens equivalent)
- Embeddings: $0.0006 / vector (512-d base embedding)
- Streaming surcharge: +10% on gen rate for real-time endpoints

2) Typical committed tiers (examples — effective per-token at commit):
- $50k/mo commit -> 12% discount (effective gen $0.00079/token)
- $120k/mo commit -> 22% discount (effective gen $0.00070/token)
- $300k+/mo -> custom pricing with SLA and burst capacity

3) How we compare vs competitors (short-form):
- OpenAI: similar baseline in non-committed scenario; OpenAI's net-effective price can be lower at very large scale but often ties to enterprise discounts. We match in latency for 2k-token median when pinned to dedicated pools.
- Anthropic: slightly higher baseline for safety-tuned models; Anthropic pricing varies by family.
- Together: cost-competitive on some models but fewer enterprise features (rollouts, SLA).
- AWS-managed LLM endpoints: higher total cost in many cases due to infra pass-through and less efficient batching; AWS strengths are region & infra control.

4) Packaging / negotiation levers to highlight to OptiCart:
- Commit size (monthly): biggest lever for unit economics.
- Model family pinning + quantization: switching to certain quantized variants reduces per-token cost.
- Routing policy: combine hosted for burst/PLG with dedicated pools for steady traffic.

5) Compliance + docs: link to SOC2 evidence and private deployment options (we provide redacted audit artifacts via secure link).

I attached a compact XLS with per-token math and example amortization across commit tiers. For external sharing, we should remove internal notes and keep the commit tiers + parity bullets. Priya — if OptiCart already told you a target commit, we can run the effective numbers and make a headline ask: "We can match OpenAI effective per-token at $X commit".

Marcus Lin
Pricing & GTM, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Amira Hassan <amira.hassan@opticart.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@opticart.com>, procurement@opticart.com, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: hosted API pricing + competitor parity request

Thanks — this is helpful and much appreciated. A few clarifications from procurement and engineering after reviewing the draft:

- OptiCart's initial expectation for a committed path is ~$120k/mo for a 12 month term (we can confirm officially in the LOI). We'd like a firm effective per-token headline at that commit (e.g., $0.0007/token) and a short note on burst capacity that avoids surprises.
- For evaluation, we still need a one-pager that we can include in the vendor matrix that states: baseline public rates, committed effective rates at $50k and $120k, and latency guidance for a 2k prompt median.
- Legal will need a short note on termination (30/60 day windows) and whether opt-outs impact committed pricing.

If you can send the one-pager + a formal quote (PDF) by EOD Tuesday, that will keep us on track for vendor selection next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — copying Daniel (CTO) in case he wants to add technical constraints.

Best,
Amira Hassan
Head of Procurement, OptiCart
